turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the data

**1. The dataset splits into three clearly different process families:**

| Family | Signature | target range |
|---|---|---|
| As-rolled / normalized only (THT=30, CT=30, TT=30) | no heat treat | 225–275 |
| Through-hardened + tempered (THT≈825–865, TT≈500–680, TCr=24) | classic Q&T | 325–930 |
| **Carburized** (NT=930, THT=30, **CT=930**, Ct>0, DT≈850–896, Dt>0, QmT 60–140, **TT=160–200, Tt=120, TCr=0.5**) | case hardening | **838–1190** |

Every sample above 930 MPa is in the carburized family, so the optimum must sit in that cluster (14 of 15 top records).

**2. Within the carburized cluster** (~25 rows), the drivers are:
- **Base C low (0.17–0.23)** — all of them; carbon comes from the case, not the core.
- **Hardenability alloying**: two equally good sub-recipes: (a) Ni≈1.6–1.7 + Cr≈0.45–0.6 + Mo≈0.16–0.21 (targets 1034, 1056, 1082, 1124, **1190**), and (b) Ni≈0.05 + Cr≈1.1–1.2 + Mo≈0.17 (1074, 1080, 1104, 1144). I take sub-recipe (a) with Cr nudged up, since it holds the single best point and both neighbours are strong → broad plateau.
- **Low P, moderate S**, Cu ≈ 0.07–0.16, Mn ≈ 0.5–0.85, Si ≈ 0.26–0.35: all weak/flat effects → put them mid-cluster (robust).
- **Ct (carburizing time)**: 90 → 540 min all give 1000+; slight benefit at high Ct. Pick ~470 (interior, flat).
- **DT/Dt (diffusion)**: (850,15), (882,25–50), (896,35–70) all appear at 1000+ → flat; pick interior (875, 35).
- **QmT**: 60 and 140 both give the top values → flat; pick 130.
- **TT/Tt/TCr**: low-temperature temper 160–200 °C, 120 min, TCr=0.5 is universal in the top rows; 160 vs 200 differs by only ~2–4% → pick 165–170, safely inside.
- **RedRatio**: 240–860 all high; 860 holds the max (1190) → pick ~800 (a ±5% move stays in a well-sampled band).
- **Inclusions dA/dB/dC**: top rows have small non-zero values (dA 0.008–0.08, dB 0–0.01, dC 0) → tiny, low sensitivity; pick small interior values, not the 0 edge.

**3. Robustness check:** every design variable I set either (i) sits inside a region where the data show a flat response (Ct, Dt, DT, QmT, TT, RedRatio, Mn, Si, Cu, P, S, dA/dB/dC), or (ii) is a categorical-like process flag defining the carburizing route (NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Tt=120, TCr=0.5) whose ±5% perturbation stays inside the same process family (e.g. CT 883–930, DT 831–919 are both covered by observed carburizing/diffusion temperatures). Composition is set mid-plateau (Ni 1.65 ±0.08, Cr 0.60 ±0.03, Mo 0.18 ±0.01, C 0.21 ±0.01 all stay inside the observed high-strength cloud), so no single 5% shift pushes the point off a ridge.

Expected performance: ~1100 ± 60 MPa, i.e. within a few percent of the observed maximum but sitting on a broad plateau rather than the single 1190 MPa spike.

**Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=470, DT=875, Dt=35, QmT=130, TT=168, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.21, Si=0.30, Mn=0.60, P=0.010, S=0.014, Ni=1.65, Cr=0.60, Cu=0.10, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=800, dA=0.05, dB=0.005, dC=0.004**
